findings.text: MMIO transport state embeds a generic virtio device, retains its platform device, retains a mapped register base, records a version number, and records whether wakeup was enabled for its shared interrupt. A helper derives the enclosing transport state from the embedded generic device.
The MMIO transport aligns newly created rings to the platform page size.
The MMIO driver emits kernel log messages under a fixed textual prefix identifying the virtio MMIO subsystem.
Transport feature negotiation preserves a fixed set of ring related feature bits and clears any other transport range bit that the ring implementation does not understand.
Notification value construction is available to transports and combines queue identity with the next available position, including wrap accounting for packed rings.
Generic ring interrupt handling is available to transports and reports whether used entries were present, honors a broken flag, marks event delivery, and invokes the queue callback when present.
Unified ring creation is available to transports and selects packed or split construction based on negotiated ring format.
Ring teardown is available to transports and detaches the queue from the device list under lock before releasing ring memory and control state.
Coherent ring memory release is available and uses a device supplied free operation when present, otherwise the generic coherent free path.

The memory device registers as a virtio driver for the memory device identifier with any sub identifier, advertises inaccessible-unplugged and persistent-suspend capabilities plus an ACPI locality capability when supported, and binds probe, remove, configuration change, freeze and restore handlers.

Probe allocates zeroed device state, initializes response waiting, work, mutex, list, spinlock and retry timer, records kdump mode, creates its queue, queries device configuration, and unless in kdump flags a configuration change and schedules background work. Failures unwind queue, mutex and allocation and clear device private data.

Removal branches on kdump mode between a vmcore oriented teardown and a hotplug oriented teardown, then resets the device, deletes queues, destroys synchronization state, frees device memory and clears device private data.

Hotplug teardown first publishes a removing state under mutex and interrupt safe spinlock, then cancels background work and timer, removes partially plugged offline blocks when in sub-block mode, unregisters device and notifier callbacks, warns if system RAM from its range remains, otherwise deletes its resource and tracking allocations.
Configuration change notification is ignored in kdump mode and otherwise flags pending configuration work and requests a retry of background processing.

Freeze refuses non-idle suspend when memory remains plugged unless persistent suspend was negotiated, otherwise resets the device, deletes queues and clears the queue pointer. Restore recreates the queue, marks the device ready and reissues configuration change handling.

Feature discovery reads high then low halves through a selector. Finalization first lets the ring layer accept features, rejects modern devices lacking first generation versioning, then publishes low and high driver feature halves through a selector.

Configuration space access on legacy version moves byte by byte for arbitrary lengths. Later versions support one two four and eight byte accesses with endian conversion, implement eight bytes as two ordered four byte register accesses, and treat any other length as fatal.

Configuration generation reads as zero on legacy version and from a generation register otherwise. Status read returns the low byte of the status register. Status write never accepts zero. Reset writes zero and on recent versions polls status until it clears.

Queue notification always reports success. The basic form signals queue identity while the data form signals a combined value derived from queue identity and next available position. Split rings use a shadow available index while packed rings fold available index and wrap counter.

The MMIO interrupt handler reads then acknowledges pending interrupt causes, forwards configuration changes to generic configuration handling, and forwards ring causes to every queue handler while accumulating handled status.

Ring interrupt handling reports no work when no used entries are present, treats broken rings as handled or optionally as unhandled with a one time warning under hardening, otherwise records event delivery and invokes the registered callback.

Single queue deletion selects the queue, deactivates it through a legacy frame register or a modern ready register with a warning if deactivation does not take effect, then performs generic ring deletion.
Deletion of all queues walks the device queue list safely, disables interrupt wakeup when it had been enabled, and releases the shared interrupt.
Callback synchronization waits for completion of the shared interrupt handler for the associated platform device.

Queue setup chooses notification style by negotiated data capability, requires a name, selects the queue, fails if already active or if maximum size reads zero, creates a ring with page alignment and owned durable memory, records maximum size, programs size and addresses, then activates. Legacy activation uses alignment plus frame number with a thirty two bit address limit while modern activation programs descriptor available and used address halves plus ready. Failures deactivate and release partial state.
Split queue creation allocates backing storage then instantiates queue state and marks the ring as owned. Instantiation failure releases the backing allocation and reports failure.

Split backing allocation requires a power of two length, warns and fails otherwise, attempts progressively smaller sizes while larger than one page when size reduction is allowed, then makes a final single page attempt before failing for lack of memory.

Ring release frees owned backing through either a mapping interface or exact page release. Packed rings release descriptor, driver event and device event areas plus descriptor tracking. Split rings release one combined area plus descriptor tracking, with tracking always released for split rings even when backing is externally owned.
Hotplug teardown serializes against online and offline activity with a hotplug mutex and publishes removal under an interrupt safe spinlock before canceling asynchronous work.
Queue list removal is serialized by the device queue list spinlock.
Unsupported configuration access widths and an attempt to set zero status are treated as fatal programming errors.
Failure of a modern queue to report inactive after deactivation is treated as a warning condition rather than a hard failure.
Legacy queue setup fails when descriptor memory lies above the addressable frame range instead of truncating the address.
Driver removal cannot reliably revoke previously added system memory, so teardown only warns when its address range still contributes system RAM.
